## Where things live

This repository is **bpmore/statamic-copydesk**, a standalone Statamic addon, developed
outside any site and linked into a host site through a Composer path repository. That is
the layout Statamic's docs recommend for an addon reused across projects.

- **This repo** (`/Users/bpmore/Herd/statamic-copydesk`) is where the code and git history live. Work happens here.
- **The host site** (`/Users/bpmore/Herd/statamic-dev`) is where anything needing a booted Statamic runs.

The host site's `composer.json` has a path repository pointing here, and Composer symlinks
it, so edits in this repo are live in the site immediately. There is **no reinstall or rebuild
step** after changing addon code.

## Target platform: do not resolve to anything older

- **Statamic:** `^6.0`. This addon targets Statamic 6. If a dependency resolves
  to `statamic/cms` 5.x, that is a bug: fix the constraint and re-resolve before doing any
  further work. Statamic 6 has a different control panel, Vue 3 + Inertia, and different
  extension points; anything built against 5.x will have to be rewritten.
- **PHP:** `^8.2`
- **Laravel / Testbench:** whatever Statamic 6 requires. Let Composer resolve it, but
  verify afterwards with `composer show statamic/cms`.

## Build commands

- Tests, from this repo: `vendor/bin/pest`
- Formatting, from this repo: `vendor/bin/pint`
- Control panel assets, from this repo: `npm install && npm run build`
- Statamic commands run from the host site, never here:
  `cd /Users/bpmore/Herd/statamic-dev && php please <command>`
- After changing `composer.json` here:
  `cd /Users/bpmore/Herd/statamic-dev && composer update bpmore/statamic-copydesk`

Do not run `php please` from this repo. There is no Statamic application here, and it
will fail.

This addon's test suite uses **Pest**. Statamic's `make:addon` scaffolds
PHPUnit and a `TestCase` extending `Statamic\Testing\AddonTestCase` (built on Orchestra
Testbench). Keep extending `AddonTestCase` whichever runner is used.

**Architecture boundary: enforce this with a test, not a convention.** The sibling
package `Bpmore\ReadabilityCore` must never import Statamic or Laravel. Keep an arch test green:

```php
arch('core stays framework-agnostic')
    ->expect('Bpmore\ReadabilityCore')
    ->not->toUse(['Statamic', 'Illuminate']);
```

## Working agreement for unattended runs

- **Read `PROGRESS.md` first.** It is the source of truth for what is done and what is next, more so than anything you remember from earlier in the session.
- **Do the next unfinished task, and only that task.** Do not run ahead into later phases, even when they look easy. Small, verified steps survive interruption; large ones don't.
- **Before you stop, always:**
  1. Update `PROGRESS.md`: tick the task, and record anything surprising under Notes.
  2. Confirm the repo builds and the test suite passes.
  3. Commit, with a message naming the task you completed.
- **Never end a task with the repo in a non-building state.** An unattended run may not resume for hours; leaving it broken wastes the whole next cycle.
- If a task turns out to be wrong or blocked, **write that under Notes in `PROGRESS.md` and stop.** Don't improvise a different plan. A stopped run with a clear note is far more useful than an autonomous detour.
- When every task is complete, put the line `ALL TASKS COMPLETE` at the top of `PROGRESS.md`.

## Compact Instructions

When compacting, preserve:

- The current state of the task list in `PROGRESS.md`
- Which files have been modified in this session
- The most recent test output and whether it passed
- Any decision recorded under Notes

## What this is

Copydesk is the addon that was called Plain until 2026-10-26. The code is Plain 1.0.1,
renamed. Nothing was sold or installed under the old name, so nothing keeps the old names
for compatibility.

- **`docs/SPEC.md`** is the Copydesk spec and **`docs/CONVENTIONS.md`** the rules every
  bpmore addon follows. Read both before starting work.
- **`docs/decision.md`** records why Copydesk is built on Plain's code, the pricing and the
  rename. **`docs/a11y-gate-plan.md`** is the plan for one publish check with A11y Gate.
- **`docs/history/`** holds Plain's own spec and progress log, for the reasons behind the
  code as it stands. They are history, not instructions.
- Copydesk's `PROGRESS.md` is written when Phase 1 is planned. Until then there is no task
  list to follow.

## Where things live: the engine

- **`packages/readability-core/`** is `bpmore/readability-core`, the framework-agnostic engine
  the addon and A11y Report both depend on. It lives in this repo with its own `composer.json`,
  `vendor/`, `phpunit.xml` and Pest suite, and has **no runtime dependencies**. Consumers take it
  through a Composer path repository. It has also been split out as its own repository,
  `github.com/bpmore/readability-core`, which matched this copy file for file on 2026-10-26
  (only `LICENSE.md` differs).
- Engine tests run from its own folder:
  `cd packages/readability-core && composer install && vendor/bin/pest` (and `vendor/bin/pint`).
- The arch test above lives in the engine's own suite (`tests/ArchTest.php`) and, because
  nothing from Statamic or Laravel is installed there, is enforced by a token scan rather than Pest's
  `toUse()`. The file says why.
- The addon's dev setup also expects Site Weather next to this folder, at
  `../statamic-site-weather`, for its tests.
